steps.title: Privilege gateway
steps.what: Because the rules are deterministic and run in the request path, inspection adds no dependency on an external service; the model layer is optional, time-boxed and circuit-broken.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Privilege console
steps.what: It is set in the Runtime Protection step of the Agent Registry wizard.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Agent key
steps.what: AI Guard is an inspection policy configured per agent key, not per app.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: External Guardrail detector and ML Sidecar
steps.what: An optional External Guardrail sends text to an operator-run HTTP service, with a URL, timeout, auth header and Block Agreement setting.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Fail Closed setting
steps.what: The screen has an Enable AI Guard switch and a Fail Closed switch, where off means fail open.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Gateway log
steps.what: AI Guard is an inspection policy configured per agent key, not per app.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Indirect injection scoring
steps.what: The Ping deck lists these AIGuard detection categories: prompt injection, jailbreak, data exfiltration, tool abuse, hidden instructions, PII, inter-agent abuse, tool poisoning, memory poisoning, malicious content, schema violation, external guardrail and indirect injection.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Graduated response
steps.what: Each policy has four outcomes: allow, alert, sanitize (redact the offending span and forward the rest) or block.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Per-category thresholds with per-key and per-…
steps.what: It also has built-in detectors, documented as 11, each with alert, sanitize and block thresholds on a 0 to 1 score, where the strongest threshold reached sets the action.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Streaming frame-by-frame inspection
steps.what: Streamed MCP responses are inspected frame by frame in real time; a flagged message is withheld while the rest of the session continues, so streaming cannot be used to avoid inspection.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Personal-data detection
steps.what: Personal-data coverage grew from 5 kinds to 23 (national identifiers, financial, health and contact details), each numeric kind checksum-validated, detected per kind, and your own formats can be pasted in unchanged in gitleaks rule format.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Public-key encrypted prompt logging
steps.what: The Ping deck lists these AIGuard detection categories: prompt injection, jailbreak, data exfiltration, tool abuse, hidden instructions, PII, inter-agent abuse, tool poisoning, memory poisoning, malicious content, schema violation, external guardrail and indirect injection.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Deterministic rule set
steps.what: The default layer is deterministic: 411 maintained rules (47 behavioural across the categories above, plus 364 secret and credential detectors), fast and explainable, with no model inference in the request path.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: Optional bring-your-own model layer
steps.what: Because the rules are deterministic and run in the request path, inspection adds no dependency on an external service; the model layer is optional, time-boxed and circuit-broken.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.

steps.title: OWASP, MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI RMF compliance…
steps.what: Every detection and policy denial is tagged to the OWASP LLM Top 10 and the OWASP Agentic Security Initiative, and cross-referenced to MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI RMF from a versioned catalog held in code, so no client or external evaluator can introduce a framework tag.
steps.why: A single gateway-wide guardrail cannot fit every caller.
